resources.string: Android asks the same “full control” question for every accessibility app. This one only uses key presses.
In the settings: tap Simple Torch Launcher, turn it on, then tap Allow.
Try it now: double-press volume up.
Try it now: double-press volume down.
It works! Double-press again to turn the torch off.
Torch off. That’s all there is to it.
Find Simple Torch Launcher, turn it on, then tap Allow.
Allow Simple Torch Launcher to have full control of your device?

Android blocks this for some apps installed outside an app store. Open App info, tap ⋮ in the top corner and choose “Allow restricted settings”. Then turn Simple Torch Launcher on in the accessibility settings again.
No torch found on this device
Single presses still change the volume, after a short delay.
Also work when the screen is off
Experimental. Works on many phones but not all, and not while music or other audio is playing.
This app is free. No ads, no tracking, no in-app purchases, and no internet access.
Free and open-source software, released under the MIT License.
Double-press a volume button to toggle the torch

Lets you double-press a volume button to turn the torch on and off.\n\nAndroid passes the app every hardware key press, like the volume buttons or a connected keyboard, but never the power button, touches or on-screen typing. The app only reacts to your chosen volume button and hands every other key straight back. It doesn’t read your screen, keeps nothing but its own settings, and has no internet access.
